reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) shows that sliding speed affects wear mechanisms and mentions friction heat and oxide layer cracking, but it provides no data on local temperature, elemental diffusion, or passive film integrity in corrosive environments. The key premises about diffusion-driven depletion and passive film degradation are unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Friction-induced heating raises local surface temperature during sliding of CoCrFeMnNi
Elevated temperature accelerates diffusion of oxide-forming elements away from the wear interface
Depletion of oxide-forming elements impairs passive film formation and repair
Impaired passive film increases susceptibility to corrosive attack, coupling wear and corrosion
Higher sliding speed increases frictional heating and thus total degradation rate
